beats.say: Your sales system, your finance system and your web shop all hold the same customer. So who makes sure they agree?

show.question: Who keeps your apps *in sync*?
show.sub: And why a hub beats a tangle

beats.say: Most companies connect their apps one pair at a time. Every link is custom work, and every link can fail on its own. An integration platform flips that: each app connects once, to a central hub.

lines.text: Each link fails on its own

beats.say: The difference grows fast. Ten apps wired directly to each other need up to forty-five links. Through a hub, they need ten.

show.head: Ten apps: links to *build and run*

beats.say: That hub is often a cloud service called an iPaaS, short for Integration Platform as a Service.

show.definition: A cloud service that connects your apps, moves data between them and *watches* every exchange.

beats.say: Sales, finance, the web shop, people data and analytics each plug into the platform once.
When an order arrives, the platform receives it, translates it into the format finance expects, routes it to the right system, and confirms delivery.

items.text: A hub: each app connects once

beats.say: Direct links multiply as you add apps.
A platform connects each app once, in one place.
And it translates, routes and watches every exchange.
Next time someone asks for a new connection, ask: should it go through the hub?

show.text: Before the next connection, ask: should it go *through the hub*?
